topics.title: Modeling Incident Account
topics.summary: A man recounts a bizarre modeling experience involving two female photographers and a motorcycle, detailing being handcuffed during the shoot and subjected to oral sex by the women due to his fantasy of being sexually assaulted. He expresses confusion about the situation and reluctance to report it.

topics.title: Real Estate Dreams and Coliseum Chaos
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, real estate buyers discuss anticipated business growth with the Dinkins administration while planning a move from New York State. The conversation quickly devolves into bizarre tangents including outlandish descriptions of Barbara Bush’s appearance (150+ years old), Howard Stern's crude commentary and discussions regarding potential expenses for a Coliseum show.

topics.title: Tennis Sponsorship & Oddities
topics.summary: During the broadcast, hosts discuss potential sponsorship opportunities for a tennis tournament while debating equipment needs and Gary’s past racquetball experiences. They also address an obsessed fan’s letters and briefly mention seeing a woman with a ball clip attached to her back during a Coliseum visit.

topics.title: Tennis Rackets, Pool Houses, & Radio Ramblings
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, hosts discuss borrowing tennis rackets from a friend with multiple sets, express skepticism about playing again, then shift to discussing extravagant home renovations like million-dollar pool house upgrades and city finances. The conversation becomes tangential involving potential mayoral candidates, criticisms of their qualifications, and an Eddie Murphy album listening session featuring some awkward impressions.

topics.title: Callers Critique Prince and Eddie Murphy
topics.summary: During the broadcast, callers express strong negative opinions about Prince’s music and appearance, dismissing his style as ‘crap.’ They speculate about his fanbase, suggesting they are “sickle cell fans,” criticizing their perceived support. The conversation then shifts to a critical assessment of Eddie Murphy's singing abilities, with callers questioning his sincerity and imitating musical styles.

topics.title: Morton Downey Jr. Parody & Listener Frustration
topics.summary: A radio segment features a parody of Jack and Michael Kay’s ‘Buttman,’ employing stereotypical LGBTQ+ depictions that sparks debate about offensive humor and listener frustration regarding perceived bias against gay people, particularly concerning immigration issues.
